newsitem.title: USA: U.S. urged to avoid clash with Europe over Cuba.
newsitem.headline: U.S. urged to avoid clash with Europe over Cuba.

text.p: Spanish Economy Minister Rodrigo Rato said on Monday the United States should avoid a clash with Europe over the restrictive Helms-Burton law against Cuba.
Rato said that Washington should use the six-month hiatus in the U.S.-European Union dispute agreed to in March to try to adapt its legislation to international standards.
"We should use the six-month delay to avoid a confrontation," he told reporters during the spring meeting of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank.

The European Union challenged the international validity of the law last year, seeking a ruling from the World Trade Organisation. But both sides decided to postpone their dispute until October to try to seek agreement.

The law, enacted in March 1996, is aimed at discouraging foreign investment in Communist-ruled Cuba. It seeks to punish foreigners who invest in assets seized after the revolution led by Fidel Castro in 1959.
Spain is one of the largest investors in Cuba.
Visiting the United Nations on Monday, Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar repeated his country's opposition to the U.S. measure and said he favoured a peaceful transition to democracy in Cuba.
"Our position on this law is the same as the rest of the European Union," he told reporters. Aznar will meet President Bill Clinton in Washington on Wednesday.
